title: Foxconn shows modular AI systems before site connection
summary: Foxconn’s HHTD26 showcase describes DSX POD preintegration and prepared-site connection. Exhibits, simulations and planned capacity remain distinct.

# Foxconn shows modular AI systems before site connection


By OpenTools Team


Foxconn’s showcase covers preintegrated systems, a simulated AI hall and a planned facility.


##


A factory‑built system still has a receiving site


Foxconn’s[October 30 announcement](https://en.prnasia.com/releases/apac/foxconn-ecosystem-enabling-token-factory-for-ai-in-spotlight-at-hon-hai-tech-day-2026-553909.shtml) describes NVIDIA DSX POD as a factory‑built reference design for preintegrating Vera Rubin rack‑scale infrastructure in modular containers. Its sequence is to complete critical validation before shipment, then connect the units to prepared site infrastructure.


The receiving site is therefore part of the handoff, rather than something the container eliminates. A buyer comparing proposals can ask which checks belong to the shipped unit and which depend on the destination being ready. A shipment acceptance record and a site‑connection record would answer different parts of that question.


##


The showcase includes a simulation and a plan


The same[release](https://en.prnasia.com/releases/apac/foxconn-ecosystem-enabling-token-factory-for-ai-in-spotlight-at-hon-hai-tech-day-2026-553909.shtml) describes an immersive simulated AI data hall, showing compute, networking, power and cooling together. It says Visionbay.ai is planning a facility design around NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS principles.


Those descriptions identify different stages of work. A reference design explains an intended integration; a simulated hall demonstrates a design concept; a facility plan precedes implementation. The announcement does not establish commissioned capacity or a measured operating result for the planned facility.


For the service layer after hardware installation, OpenTools’[enterprise‑system‑design reference](https://opentools.ai/resources/enterprise-system-design) covers serving, admission control, observability and partial failures. That broader operational checklist complements a hardware handoff; it is not documentation for DSX POD or its site requirements.


IBM Portable Modular Data Center on a trailer, photographed September 22, 2011. An archival example of transportable computing, not Foxconn equipment.
